messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> page fired for high 5xx rate on /api/generate (service: inference-frontend). Alert threshold: >1.5% 5xx over 1m.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-071 opened and assigned to maya (primary on-call). Severity: P1.
maya: acked. I'm looking. Any customer reports?
sam: Not yet but getting a couple of errors from prod-monitoring channel. Started ~12:02 UTC.
jordan: seeing a spike in 5xx from one AZ (us-west-2b). Traffic looks normal but error ratio high.
maya: thanks. can someone run a quick query to see error types? `curl -s 'https://logs.internal/query?service=inference-frontend&since=5m' | jq '.errors|group_by(.code)|map({code:.[0].code,count:length})'`
alex: I can take a look in ~8 mins, want a handoff? maya: please take it, i need to step into a call in 5. i'll handoff to alex.
maya: Handoff -> alex. Notes: spike started 12:02 UTC, errors are largely 502/504, concentrated on host pool gpu-pool-3, increased queue backlog. Cache hit rate normal. No config deploys in last 30m.
alex: acked and taking over. ping me if anything else. -alex
ops-bot: auto-escalation timer set for 10m.
alex: digging into runtime logs now. seeing repeated "UpstreamReadTimeout" from model-worker-3 instances.
sam: correlated with a slight CPU saturation on model-worker-3, metrics: cpu 95% for last 2m.
alex: scaling group shows no recent autoscale event, autoscaler reports `suppressing_additional_nodes` due to policy. That might be blocking scale-up.
jordan: trying a temporary manual scale to add 2 instances to gpu-pool-3.
alex: go ahead. also rotating some traffic away from that AZ: `route override add --service inference-frontend --target region:us-west-2a,us-west-2c --weight 50%`
jordan: traffic rebalanced. manual scale initiated (+2 workers).
pagerduty-bot: alex acknowledged INC-2026-071 and set status to "investigating".
alex: monitoring 5xx after scale and drain. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/inference/5xx?from=now-5m (sharing)
sam: initial drop from 2.1% -> 0.6% after partial drain, still seeing some 502s for in-flight requests.
alex: running canary route: drain instance model-worker-3-7, then restart process there.
ops-bot: restart job scheduled for model-worker-3-7 by alex. ETA 30s.
alex: restarted process, health checks passing. model-worker-3-7 back in pool.
sam: tailing logs: 502s reduced to baseline 0.12%.
maya: great work. any customer-facing impact? estimated affected requests: ~0.8% of requests for 12:02-12:10 UTC, latency unchanged for successful requests.
jordan: no open support tickets flagged yet. monitoring team sent advisory to cs-team just in case.
alex: leaving note to revise autoscaler suppression policy; filed ticket INFRA-2274.
alex: closing actions: 1) remove suppression rule, 2) add autorestart on `UpstreamReadTimeout` spikes, 3) add a runbook step to scale pool manually.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-071 moved to "stabilized" by alex.
maya: thanks alex + team. i'll follow up with postmortem draft. tagging @oncall-sre for review.
alex: ending handoff — i'll be on standby for next 30m. :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-071 update: status=stabilized, duration=18m, severity=P1, leads=[maya,alex].
maya: postmortem checklist: collect logs, timeline, impacted customer count, mitigation steps, followups (INFRA-2274). i'll own the writeup.
sam: marking this thread resolved on slack after postmortem.
